Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Boyolali Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regent...................
-3-
4. Regent is the Regent of Boyolali.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administrator.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region.
7. Regional Technical Implementation Unit is a technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, exploitation, discrimination, who require special protection, and other problems.
8. Integrated Service Center is a non-structural institution that coordinates the implementation of an integrated service system for women victims.
9. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of humans as creatures of God Almighty and are His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
10. Women's Empowerment is all efforts to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
11. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as fulfilling their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of Human Rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
13. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
14. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
15. Violence....................
-4-
15. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differentiation that results in, or could result in physical, psychological and/or sexual suffering to women, including threats, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of private life.
16. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of Human Rights caused by gender role labeling based on gender, which denies human dignity and the right to self that has an impact on, or has an impact similar to physical, psychological, and sexual or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life.
17. Disaster is an event or series of events that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of the community caused by natural and/or non-natural factors as well as human factors resulting in human casualties, environmental damage, property losses, and psychological impacts.
18. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman.
19. Elderly is a person who has reached the age of 60 (sixty) years and above.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
21. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
22. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for the Community.
23. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
24. Data and Information System is the collection, management, and utilization of Women's data needed in the Implementation of Women's Protection and Empowerment.

Letter a What is meant by "the principle of respect for Human Rights" is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women's rights as part of Human Rights.

Letter c What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is that in the protection and empowerment of women it is carried out without regard to differences whether in the dimension of territory (disaster areas, conflict areas, border areas, underdeveloped areas, remote areas, and others), the dimension of age (productive age, elderly age, and others), and special dimensions (persons with disabilities, workers, and others).
Letter d What is meant by "the principle of victim protection" is that the protection and empowerment of women carried out by the Regional Government, business entities or the community is oriented towards the protection of women as victims.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BOYOLALI REGENCY
NUMBER YEAR 2021
CONCERNING
PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and Regional Government in accordance with their authority is responsible for respecting, protecting, and guaranteeing the human rights of every citizen including women and children without discrimination, because women and children are part of Indonesian citizens who have the same rights as others, and the rights of women and children are human rights that must be guaranteed, protected not only by the government but also by the Regional Government.
Although there are guarantees in laws and regulations that protect citizens, especially women, cases involving women continue to increase, not decrease, because cases of violence against women are like an iceberg phenomenon, namely cases reported to women's protection institutions are only a small part of the actual cases. Women victims of violence often feel hesitant or afraid to report the violence they experience, or there are other obstacles such as difficulty in accessing services and lack of information about their rights because most women victims come from poor and underprivileged families, so they need assistance, assistance costs, and legal consultation is expensive. On the other hand, institutions that handle women's protection are still lacking, especially in areas far from the city center.
Various forms of acts of violence, mistreatment, exploitation, and neglect of Women that occur in the Region require strategic efforts from the Regional Government to provide protection for women.
Furthermore, in order to realize regional policies to administer governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region in the field of women's protection based on Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times most recently by Law Number 11 of 2020 concerning Job Creation, it is necessary to formulate this in a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation is a concrete manifestation of the Boyolali Regency Government in providing protection and guaranteeing the fulfillment of the human rights of Women in accordance with its duties and responsibilities.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BOYOLALI REGENCY
NUMBER YEAR 2021
CONCERNING
PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and Regional Government in accordance with their authority is responsible for respecting, protecting, and guaranteeing the human rights of every citizen including women and children without discrimination, because women and children are part of Indonesian citizens who have the same rights as others, and the rights of women and children are human rights that must be guaranteed, protected not only by the government but also by the Regional Government.
Although there are guarantees in laws and regulations that protect citizens, especially women, cases involving women continue to increase, not decrease, because cases of violence against women are like an iceberg phenomenon, namely cases reported to women's protection institutions are only a small part of the actual cases. Women victims of violence often feel hesitant or afraid to report the violence they experience, or there are other obstacles such as difficulty in accessing services and lack of information about their rights because most women victims come from poor and underprivileged families, so they need assistance, assistance costs, and legal consultation is expensive. On the other hand, institutions that handle women's protection are still lacking, especially in areas far from the city center.
Various forms of acts of violence, mistreatment, exploitation, and neglect of Women that occur in the Region require strategic efforts from the Regional Government to provide protection for women.
Furthermore, in order to realize regional policies to administer governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region in the field of women's protection based on Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times most recently by Law Number 11 of 2020 concerning Job Creation, it is necessary to formulate this in a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation is a concrete manifestation of the Boyolali Regency Government in providing protection and guaranteeing the fulfillment of the human rights of Women in accordance with its duties and responsibilities.

Women victims of violence often feel hesitant or afraid to report the violence they experience, or there are other obstacles such as difficulty in accessing services and lack of information about their rights because most women victims come from poor and underprivileged families, so they need assistance, assistance costs, and legal consultation is expensive. On the other hand, institutions that handle women's protection are still lacking, especially in areas far from the city center.
Various forms of acts of violence, mistreatment, exploitation, and neglect of Women that occur in the Region require strategic efforts from the Regional Government to provide protection for women.
Furthermore, in order to realize regional policies to administer governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region in the field of women's protection based on Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times most recently by Law Number 11 of 2020 concerning Job Creation, it is necessary to formulate this in a Regional Regulation.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and Regional Government in accordance with their authority is responsible for respecting, protecting, and guaranteeing the human rights of every citizen including women and children without discrimination, because women and children are part of Indonesian citizens who have the same rights as others, and the rights of women and children are human rights that must be guaranteed, protected not only by the government but also by the Regional Government.
Although there are guarantees in laws and regulations that protect citizens, especially women, cases involving women continue to increase, not decrease, because cases of violence against women are like an iceberg phenomenon, namely cases reported to women's protection institutions are only a small part of the actual cases. Women victims of violence often feel hesitant or afraid to report the violence they experience, or there are other obstacles such as difficulty in accessing services and lack of information about their rights because most women victims come from poor and underprivileged families, so they need assistance, assistance costs, and legal consultation is expensive. On the other hand, institutions that handle women's protection are still lacking, especially in areas far from the city center.
Various forms of acts of violence, mistreatment, exploitation, and neglect of Women that occur in the Region require strategic efforts from the Regional Government to provide protection for women.
Furthermore, in order to realize regional policies to administer governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region in the field of women's protection based on Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times most recently by Law Number 11 of 2020 concerning Job Creation, it is necessary to formulate this in a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation is a concrete manifestation of the Boyolali Regency Government in providing protection and guaranteeing the fulfillment of the human rights of Women in accordance with its duties and responsibilities.

On the other hand, institutions that handle women's protection are still lacking, especially in areas far from the city center.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL
The State through the government and Regional Government in accordance with their authority is responsible for respecting, protecting, and guaranteeing the human rights of every citizen including women and children without discrimination, because women and children are part of Indonesian citizens who have the same rights as others, and the rights of women and children are human rights that must be guaranteed, protected not only by the government but also by the Regional Government.
Although there are guarantees in laws and regulations that protect citizens, especially women, cases involving women continue to increase, not decrease, because cases of violence against women are like an iceberg phenomenon, namely cases reported to women's protection institutions are only a small part of the actual cases. Women victims of violence often feel hesitant or afraid to report the violence they experience, or there are other obstacles such as difficulty in accessing services and lack of information about their rights because most women victims come from poor and underprivileged families, so they need assistance, assistance costs, and legal consultation is expensive. On the other hand, institutions that handle women's protection are still lacking, especially in areas far from the city center.
Various forms of acts of violence, mistreatment, exploitation, and neglect of Women that occur in the Region require strategic efforts from the Regional Government to provide protection for women.
Furthermore, in order to realize regional policies to administer governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region in the field of women's protection based on Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times most recently by Law Number 11 of 2020 concerning Job Creation, it is necessary to formulate this in a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation is a concrete manifestation of the Boyolali Regency Government in providing protection and guaranteeing the fulfillment of the human rights of Women in accordance with its duties and responsibilities.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BOYOLALI REGENCY
NUMBER YEAR 2021
CONCERNING
PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and Regional Government in accordance with their authority is responsible for respecting, protecting, and guaranteeing the human rights of every citizen including women and children without discrimination, because women and children are part of Indonesian citizens who have the same rights as others, and the rights of women and children are human rights that must be guaranteed, protected not only by the government but also by the Regional Government.
Although there are guarantees in laws and regulations that protect citizens, especially women, cases involving women continue to increase, not decrease, because cases of violence against women are like an iceberg phenomenon, namely cases reported to women's protection institutions are only a small part of the actual cases. Women victims of violence often feel hesitant or afraid to report the violence they experience, or there are other obstacles such as difficulty in accessing services and lack of information about their rights because most women victims come from poor and underprivileged families, so they need assistance, assistance costs, and legal consultation is expensive. On the other hand, institutions that handle women's protection are still lacking, especially in areas far from the city center.
Various forms of acts of violence, mistreatment, exploitation, and neglect of Women that occur in the Region require strategic efforts from the Regional Government to provide protection for women.
Furthermore, in order to realize regional policies to administer governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region in the field of women's protection based on Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times most recently by Law Number 11 of 2020 concerning Job Creation, it is necessary to formulate this in a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation is a concrete manifestation of the Boyolali Regency Government in providing protection and guaranteeing the fulfillment of the human rights of Women in accordance with its duties and responsibilities.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BOYOLALI REGENCY
NUMBER YEAR 2021
CONCERNING
PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and Regional Government in accordance with their authority is responsible for respecting, protecting, and guaranteeing the human rights of every citizen including women and children without discrimination, because women and children are part of Indonesian citizens who have the same rights as others, and the rights of women and children are human rights that must be guaranteed, protected not only by the government but also by the Regional Government.
Although there are guarantees in laws and regulations that protect citizens, especially women, cases involving women continue to increase, not decrease, because cases of violence against women are like an iceberg phenomenon, namely cases reported to women's protection institutions are only a small part of the actual cases. Women victims of violence often feel hesitant or afraid to report the violence they experience, or there are other obstacles such as difficulty in accessing services and lack of information about their rights because most women victims come from poor and underprivileged families, so they need assistance, assistance costs, and legal consultation is expensive. On the other hand, institutions that handle women's protection are still lacking, especially in areas far from the city center.
Various forms of acts of violence, mistreatment, exploitation, and neglect of Women that occur in the Region require strategic efforts from the Regional Government to provide protection for women.
Furthermore, in order to realize regional policies to administer governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region in the field of women's protection based on Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times most recently by Law Number 11 of 2020 concerning Job Creation, it is necessary to formulate this in a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation is a concrete manifestation of the Boyolali Regency Government in providing protection and guaranteeing the fulfillment of the human rights of Women in accordance with its duties and responsibilities.

13. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.

15. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differentiation that results in, or could result in physical, psychological and/or sexual suffering to women, including threats, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of private life.
16. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of Human Rights caused by gender role labeling based on gender, which denies human dignity and the right to self that has an impact on, or has an impact similar to physical, psychological, and sexual or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life.
17. Disaster is an event or series of events that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of the community caused by natural and/or non-natural factors as well as human factors resulting in human casualties, environmental damage, property losses, and psychological impacts.

19. Elderly is a person who has reached the age of 60 (sixty) years and above.
20. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
21. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
22. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for the Community.
23. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
24. Data and Information System is the collection, management, and utilization of Women's data needed in the Implementation of Women's Protection and Empowerment.
